evidence.quote:
Methods: This study introduces a hybrid AI-driven diagnostic framework that 
integrates an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) trained on clinical data from 1,200 
patients using 31 demographic, symptomatic, and behavioral features with a 
Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on 4,876 MRI images to classify 
AD into four stages.
evidence.point: Establishes the clinical ANN and MRI CNN populations and the CNN’s four-stage classification task.

evidence.quote:
Results and Discussion:  The ANN achieved an accuracy of 87.08% in early-
stage risk prediction, while the CNN demonstrated a superior 97% accuracy in 
disease staging, supported by Grad-CAM visualizations that improved model 
interpretability.
evidence.point: Directly supports both reported accuracies and their distinct endpoints.

evidence.quote:
This study utilized two publicly available Kaggle datasets to 
develop a dual-model diagnostic framework for Alzheimer’s disease. 
The first dataset contains 4,876 MRI brain images, used to train the 
CNN model, while the second dataset includes clinical data from 
1,200 patients, used to train the ANN model.
evidence.point: Confirms separate public datasets; the figures do not establish a head-to-head comparison on a common clinical population and endpoint.

output.rationale: The values, model assignments, populations and task distinctions are supported by the abstract and dataset description. No prediction horizon is inferred. I agree that the unrelated ARG forbidden-conflation text is a minor annotation defect, but classify its severity as non_blocking under the supplied definitions rather than none. The scoring key can stand unchanged.
output.correction_assessment: The proposed correction is appropriate. Replace the ARG boilerplate with a warning against treating these accuracies as a head-to-head comparison of clinical diagnostic performance across the same population and endpoint.
